It presents the same decentralization policy, identifies the Joint Federal-State Action Committee, specifically describes its recommendation concerning State assumption of peacetime atomic-energy functions, and calls for the federal and State actions that culminated in the statute and implementation process discussed by the child. The child reuses that policy narrative and adapts it from a request for legislation into a request that Governors review the Atomic Energy Commission's proposed transfer criteria. C16 is a meaningful but more general precursor establishing the committee and its transfer-of-functions framework; C10 shares the Governor/AEC consultation format but concerns reactor development rather than transfer of regulatory authority.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"I have often stressed the need to increase the functions and responsibilities of the States as a safeguard against excessive centralization of governmental power in this country.","parent_excerpt":"On numerous occasions I have warned against the dangers of overcentralizing power and authority in the National Government. Similarly have I made clear my deep conviction that to avoid these dangers State and local governments must be strengthened.","explanation":"Distinctive parallel framing presents increased State responsibility as the remedy for excessive federal centralization."},{"child_excerpt":"Public Law 86-373 was enacted in response to a recommendation by the Joint Federal-State Action Committee.","parent_excerpt":"To carry out the fourth recommendation the Chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission will suggest such revisions as are appropriate in the language of the pending proposal on peacetime uses of atomic energy.","explanation":"The parent identifies the same committee recommendation and the atomic-energy legislative proposal that became the law implemented in the child."},{"child_excerpt":"The law authorizes the Atomic Energy Commission to enter into agreements with the Governors of the States under which the States will assume responsibility for specified regulatory functions now performed by the Commission","parent_excerpt":"Enactment at this time of federal legislation would be an encouraging step in the effort to strengthen State governments, by restoring to them specific functions... To give full effect to the Committee's recommendations the States, through their Governors and Legislatures, will also have to act.","explanation":"Both use the same administrative machinery: federal legislation implementing committee recommendations, followed by State action to assume functions previously performed federally."}]}
